questions.questionsTitle: A1. Simple Factual Activity: Say whether the following statements are True or False

subQuestion.question: (1) The sages say that life is a dark dream.
subQuestion.ans: True

subQuestion.question: (2) The clouds of gloom are permanent.
subQuestion.ans: False

subQuestion.question: (3) We must enjoy the happy hours of our life.
subQuestion.ans: True

subQuestion.question: (4) Life's sunny hours flit by quickly.
subQuestion.ans: True

subQuestion.question: (1) What do the sages say?
subQuestion.ans: The sages say that life is a dark dream.

subQuestion.question: (2) What does the rain often foretell?
subQuestion.ans: The rain often foretells a pleasant day.

subQuestion.question: (3) What should we do during the joyful times in life?
subQuestion.ans: We should enjoy the joyful times of our life gratefully and cheerfully.

subQuestion.question: (4) Complete the following: We should not be unhappy when we have difficulties because ……
subQuestion.ans: We should not be unhappy when we have difficulties because these difficulties are temporary. If we have difficulties at some stage in our lives, there will be joyous times following it later.

questions.questionsTitle: A3. Activities based on Poetic Devices

subQuestion.question: (1) Pick out from the extract two lines each that reflect an optimistic (positive) attitude and pessimistic (negative) attitude.
subQuestion.ans:
Optimism:
(1) Foretells a pleasant day.
(2) But these are transient all.
Pessimism:
(1) Oft a little morning rain.
(2) Sometimes there are clouds of gloom.

subQuestion.question: (2a) Explain the metaphor in the following lines: Oft a little morning rain Foretells a pleasant day.
subQuestion.ans: If we have difficulties at some stage, there will be joyous times following it. Difficulties are implicitly compared to rain and joyous times to a pleasant day.

subQuestion.question: (2b) Explain the metaphor: Sometimes there are clouds.
subQuestion.ans: Sometimes there are problems. Problems are implicitly compared to clouds.

subQuestion.question: (2c) Explain the metaphor: …the shower will make the roses bloom.
subQuestion.ans: The problems we face will make for better times ahead. Problems are implicitly compared to the showers of rain and better times are implicitly compared to roses blooming.

subQuestion.question: (2d) Explain the metaphor: Life's sunny hours flit by.
subQuestion.ans: The happy times of our life go by very quickly. Here, the happy times are implicitly compared to sunny hours.

subQuestion.question: (2e) Pick out an example of interrogation (rhetorical question) from the extract. Explain in your own words the point that it makes.
subQuestion.ans: Interrogation : If the shower will make the roses bloom. Oh, why lament its fall? /n Explanation: If a little rain helps , the roses to flower, weshould not feel unhappyabout it. Thismeansthat we must not expressregret for the difficultieswe face in life.

questions.questionsTitle: Simple Factual Activity - Complete the following

subQuestion.question: (1) One should bear the day of trial _______ and _______.
subQuestion.ans: courageously and fearlessly

subQuestion.question: (2) The wings of hope are _______ and _______.
subQuestion.ans: golden and buoyant (strong, elastic)

subQuestion.question: (1) Does sorrow actually win over hope, according to the poet?
subQuestion.ans: No. Though hope is temporarily defeated, it springs up again and helps us to bear the days of trials.

subQuestion.question: (2) Who does 'Our Best' refer to?
subQuestion.ans: 'Our Best' refers to those whom we love and cherish the most.

subQuestion.question: (3) Why are the wings of hope 'golden'?
subQuestion.ans: Gold is the colour of optimism. The wings of hope are golden because hope helps us bear up with our problems and suppress despair.

subQuestion.question: (1) Pick out from the extract two lines each that reflect an optimistic attitude and pessimistic attitude.
subQuestion.ans: Optimism: (1) Yet Hope again elastic springs. (2) Still buoyant are her golden wings. Pessimism: (1) What though death at times steps in, And calls our Best away? (2) What though Sorrow seems to win, O'er hope a heavy sway?

subQuestion.question: (2) Pick out four examples of personification from the extract. Write what is personified in each.
subQuestion.ans: (1) 'Death steps in.' Death is personified. (2) 'Sorrow seems to win.' Sorrow is personified. (3) 'Yet Hope again elastic springs, Unconquered though she fell.' Hope is personified. (4) 'Can courage quell despair!' Courage is personified.

subQuestion.question: (3) Pick out two examples of interrogation (rhetorical questions) from the extract. Explain in your own words the point that each one makes.

subAns.Interrogation: (1) What though death at times steps in, And calls our Best away? (2) What though Sorrow seems to win, O'er hope a heavy sway?
subAns.Explanation: (1) If death, at times takes away the people we love most. We must accept it and hope for better times. (2) It does not matter if we are overcome by sorrow and hope seems to be far away.

subQuestion.question: Think and write down three or four ways in which we can express the idea of 'death' in a tactful and gentle manner.
subQuestion.ans: (1) The person has left for his heavenly abode. (2) He/She has gone to meet his/her Maker. (3) He/She has become the beloved of God. (4) He/She has completed his work on this earth.

subQuestion.question: '….. and that's how I realized that courage and hope can help me overcome any major mishap/problem in life.' Write an episode/experience from your own life that leads to the above conclusion.
subQuestion.ans: I am a lover of sports. My favourite game is football. I wanted to play in my school team, and right from the age of eleven, I had been practising very sincerely. Then one unfortunate day, when I was twelve, I fell down the stairs of my building and fractured my leg badly. I was devastated. How could I play my favourite game? How could I make it to the team? Would my leg ever become completely alright again? Would I be able to run around and kick the ball as before? I felt that my world had ended. This was the time when my family gave me their full support. My grandparents helped me to while away the long hours; my parents made nutritious food for me and saw to the medical treatment. My sister, who is four years older than me, gave me sound advice and courage. She understood what I was going through. She told me of various people who had suffered terrible disasters and had risen above them. She brought me videos of umpteen cases where the mind had won over the body. She made me read biographies of achievers like Wilma Rudolph and Sudha Chandran. She made me do my exercises regularly and keep in touch with my sport. Slowly but surely, I regained courage and confidence. Believe it or not, two years later I made it to my football team! My doctor and my family said that it was optimism and a positive attitude that had helped me recover completely. And that's how I realized that courage and hope can help me (or anybody) overcome any major mishap/problem in life.
